source: Republique du Benin, Ministere de la Sante - Plan d'endiguement du cholera au Benin 2017-2021 (juin 2017)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2016-01-01..2016-12-31. Source states: 'Elle a touche principalement les communes de So-Ava, des Aguegues, d'Adjohoun et de Dangbo... L'epidemie s'est etendue dans les communes d'Aguegue, Adjohoun, Dangbo, Bonou et Ze... Les communes touchees au cours de cette flambee sont : Cotonou, Abomey-Calavi, So-Ava, Allada, Ze, Ouidah, Seme-Podji, Adjarra, Bohicon, Abomey, Dassa-Zounme, Savalou, Bante, Save, Parakou et N'dali'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. DEPARTMENT-LEVEL ABSENCE FOR Couffo, 2016, derived from a COMPLETE POSITIVE ENUMERATION by the national authority, not from table omission. The Benin Ministry of Health's Plan d'Endiguement du Cholera 2017-2021 (June 2017), section 1.5, states 'L'annee 2016 a ete marquee par DEUX flambees epidemiques de cholera' and then names the communes affected by each. First wave (weeks 5-24, 196 cases, 0 deaths): So-Ava, Aguegues, Adjohoun, Dangbo, Bonou, Ze. Second wave (weeks 32-46, 678 cases, 13 deaths): Cotonou, Abomey-Calavi, So-Ava, Allada, Ze, Ouidah, Seme-Kpodji, Adjarra, Bohicon, Abomey, Dassa-Zoume, Savalou, Bante, Save, Parakou, N'Dali, plus Porto-Novo in the narrative. Mapping those communes to departments gives exactly six affected departments - Atlantique, Oueme, Littoral, Zou, Collines, Borgou - and six with no affected commune: Alibori, Atacora, Couffo, Donga, Mono, Plateau. Couffo is in the second group, so it recorded no cholera case in either 2016 wave and, because the ministry states the year consisted of those two waves only, none in 2016 at all. INDEPENDENT CONSISTENCY CHECK: the six affected departments are precisely the six that already carry sub-national 2016 rows in this file (Atlantique, Borgou, Collines, Littoral, Oueme, Zou, from the UNICEF 22 Sep 2016 sitrep and the JHU UID 3541 commune table), and no source at any level places a 2016 case in Couffo. With these six rows all twelve Benin departments are now accounted for in 2016. SURVEILLANCE STATUS: partial, and deliberately so - the same ministry document records concrete 2016 surveillance failures ('il est apparu des dysfonctionnements au niveau du systeme de surveillance epidemiologique et de la confirmation biologique'): the index death of the second wave occurred on 9 August at So-Ava but was notified to the health zone only on 17 August and nationally on 19 August; early Cotonou cases were treated in private practices that made no notification; community cases went unrecorded; sample transport to the national reference laboratory failed in all health zones and the laboratory ran out of reagents. Confidence is therefore held at 0.7 rather than the 0.8 that CLAUDE.md allows a government report, because a surveillance system that missed a week of transmission in its epicentre could also have missed a small number of cases in a quiet department. REGIONAL CROSS-CHECK: 2016 was NOT a regionally quiet year - Benin's own national total was 874 cases across the two waves and neighbouring Togo and Nigeria were both reporting cholera - so this is an absence asserted during regional activity and is weighted accordingly. DOUBLE-COUNTING: provincial subset of the 2016 national rows (AI rows 5, 79, 80) - do not sum with them; it contributes zero cases either way.
